scenes.beat: Dev hands Leo a coffee mug / a cup of tea with the name 'Leonard' written on it while someone knocking on the door of the portable restroom startles Leo in the background. Boss Greg stands nearby giving a blank stare as Leo insists his hyper-expensive gear makes him a pro athlete.

story.title: Why Expensive Gear Doesn't Save You 🏃
story.insight: Spent four hundred bucks on socks just to quit at mile one.
story.caption: Leo spent four hundred dollars on running gear to prove he has his life together.

shots.scene: Leo and Mia sit at the podcast desk near the park starting line. Dev stands in the background holding a coffee mug / a cup of tea. Leo grips his neon water bottle.

lines.text: These four hundred dollar shoes practically run the race for me!
Too bad your legs gave up during the stretch.

shots.scene: Dev hands Leo the coffee mug / a cup of tea with 'Leonard' misspelled on it. Boss Greg stands nearby giving a blank stare. Leo glares at his shoes.

lines.text: Kyle just texted: real runners drink raw butter.
Kyle lost to a kid on a tricycle.

shots.scene: Someone knocking on the door of a portable restroom in the background startles Leo. Mia clicks her handheld tally counter with a sharp grin.

lines.text: Wait- was that the horn or my stomach collapsing?
That's point one hundred and fifty for my scoreboard!

shots.scene: Leo drops his fancy water bottle on the desk with a loud clatter. Greg stares harder from the background. Mia sips her drink calmly.

lines.text: This is worse than the pineapple pizza incident.
You've been standing still for three whole minutes.

shots.scene: Leo leans forward over the desk, frantically adjusting his neon headband while Dev watches from behind. Mia clicks her counter again.

lines.text: Okay but hear me out, what if I buy faster socks?
Anyway. We made it through season one together, buddy.

shots.scene: Leo stares directly into the camera with wide terrified eyes, clutching his knees. Mia points a thumb at him.

lines.text: Next season I am buying six hundred dollar shoes!

scenes.setting: Park finish line bench
scenes.beat: Leo crosses the finish line dead last, immediately pulling the blanket / pillow / lying in bed on a park bench while nosy neighbor Brenda holds a clipboard in victory. Mia clicks her scoreboard to 150, hands him a slice of pineapple pizza, and admits he actually stuck to his plan.

story.title: Why Horrible Runs Feel Amazingly Good 🏃
story.insight: We judge an entire experience by its peak and how it ends.
story.caption: Leo survived his 5K race for free pizza. Here is why his brain thinks he won gold!

shots.scene: Both sit at cozy podcast desk. Leo is dramatically pulling the blanket / pillow / lying in bed across his chair with exhausted eyes. Mia smirks nearby.

lines.text: I survived a brutal five-kilometer death march today, bro!

shots.scene: Both sit at podcast desk. Mia clicks her handheld counter while a digital clock showing a time sits between them. Leo sits up, frowning slightly.

lines.text: You crawled three blocks and took two juice box naps.
That is number one hundred fifty on my scoreboard!

shots.scene: Both sit at cozy podcast desk. Mia holds a coffee mug / a cup of tea and a pizza slice, smiling. Leo reaches over with wide curious eyes.

lines.text: Okay but hear me out, the finish line had pizza.
It is pineapple pizza, your absolute nemesis.

shots.scene: Podcast desk set. Nosy neighbor Brenda is visible in background walking / pacing the hallway trail with a clipboard. Leo smirks with closed lips.

lines.text: Best morning of my entire adult life, dude!
You literally cried behind a dumpster at minute forty-two.

shots.scene: Both sit at podcast desk while an alarm going off signals on the table. Mia hands him the food with a soft smile. Leo looks touched.

lines.text: Ending with warm cheese makes the misery totally worth it.
Honestly? You didn't quit. I am proud of you.

shots.scene: Both sit at podcast desk as someone knocking on the door sounds in background. Leo tilts his head with an expectant closed-mouth grin.

lines.text: Does this mean I have my life together now?
